claims.claim: eftpos is Australia's domestic debit card network, operated by Australian Payments Plus (AP+) since the 2021 amalgamation of eftpos, BPAY Group and NPPA (ACCC approval 9 September 2021).
claims.quote: The ACCC has authorised the amalgamation of BPAY Group, eftpos and NPPA to form Australian Payments Plus
claims.title: eftpos Australia
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: News list on the eftpos page; ACCC approval item dated 9 September 2021; proposal announced 15 December 2020; inaugural CEO Lynn Kraus appointed 22 December 2021. No ownership change since found. HQ: AP+ is Sydney-based (Gadigal land acknowledgement).

claims.claim: AP+ states eftpos is available on over 70 million debit cards.
claims.quote: eftpos is Australia’s local debit card network, available on over 70 million debit cards and securely processing payments behind the scenes.
claims.title: eftpos Australia
claims.label: Vendor
claims.note: Flag: the MCR and accepting-payments pages cite 'over 50 million contactless enabled MND cards' (source 'eftpos statistics, June 2025'); different metric (all debit vs contactless multi-network).

claims.claim: AP+ cites over 50 million contactless-enabled multi-network debit cards in Australia (eftpos statistics, June 2025).
claims.quote: There are over 50 million³ contactless enabled MND cards in Australia, featuring both eftpos and an international card network.
claims.title: Merchant Choice Routing - eftpos
claims.label: Vendor
claims.note: Footnote 3: eftpos statistics, June 2025.

claims.claim: AP+ claimed eftpos had around 35% share of online debit card payments as at July 2024 (AP+ CNP volume 47.9m vs RBA table).
claims.quote: it now has around 35% share of all debit card payments made online
claims.title: Rollout of Merchant Choice Routing for mobile devices plus lower eftpos debit charges will lower the cost of payments in Australia
claims.label: Vendor
claims.note: Footnote 3: AP+ eftpos card not present volumes July 2024 47.9m.

claims.claim: eftpos members include banks, fintechs and retailers; recent members announced include Worldpay from FIS (6 July 2023) and J.P. Morgan Payments (25 July 2024).
claims.quote: eftpos’ diverse Members include banks, FinTechs and retailers – giving eftpos the combined skills to solve local payment problems in new ways.
claims.title: Members and partners - eftpos
claims.label: Vendor
claims.note: No member count published on the page; the AP+ 'Scheme members' page rendered only introductory text in curl (member list likely JS-rendered).

claims.claim: eftpos offers merchants/acquirers fraud prevention, tokenisation, EMV 3DS strong customer authentication, and stand-in processing (STIP) for issuer outages.
claims.quote: eftpos offers stand-in processing (STIP) capability that can authorise and process payments if the cardholder’s bank is unreachable
claims.title: eftpos Australia
claims.label: Vendor
claims.note: Same page lists Fraud prevention, Tokenisation services, PCI DSS compliance, Strong customer authentication (EMV 3DS).

claims.claim: STIP became optional for eftpos issuers from October 2025; a Phase 2 with enhanced checks is on the July 2026 roadmap.
claims.quote: stand-in processing capability that operates when issuer systems are unreachable from the eftpos hub, adding resiliency to debit card transaction processing.
claims.title: AP+ Roadmap (31 July 2026)
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Page continues: 'Optional for eftpos issuers from October 2025.' Roadmap also lists eftpos Click to Pay, eftpos In-App Payments (Apple Pay pilot Sept 2025), 3DS 2.3 update, 3DES-to-AES migration by 2030.

claims.claim: For merchants the MCR page lists eftpos fraud features: EMV 3DS, real-time fraud scoring and automated disputes and chargebacks; MCR is arranged via the merchant's acquirer/PSP, not directly with AP+.
claims.quote: Merchants and cardholders can benefit from eftpos’ fraud protection features including EMV 3DS, real-time fraud scoring, and automated disputes and chargebacks.
claims.title: Merchant Choice Routing - eftpos
claims.label: Vendor
claims.note: Get started: 'contact your banking partner, payment service provider, or AP+ relationship manager'.

claims.claim: eftpos Click to Pay is announced as 'launching soon' for online multi-network debit with integrated MCR and tokenisation; Tap to Pay on iPhone/Android partners named (ANZ Worldline, Tyro, Westpac EFTPOS AIR, NAB Easy Tap, Square).
claims.quote: eftpos Click to Pay is launching soon in a world-first for online multi-network debit (MND) card payments.
claims.title: Accepting payments - eftpos
claims.label: Vendor
claims.note: Dec 2025 roadmap: Click to Pay parity mandate from 2027 for institutions supporting Click to Pay with international schemes.

claims.claim: AP+ operates three partner portals: a ServiceNow Member Portal (members.auspayplus.com.au/csm, login required), the eftpos brand portal, and the AP+ Developers portal.
claims.quote: Portals Member portal Brand portal Developer portal
claims.title: eftpos Australia
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Member portal fetched: 'Member Portal Login - AP+ Member Portal' – login wall. Brand portal (brandportaleftpos.auspayplus.com.au) rendered only a title in curl (JS app).

claims.claim: The Dec 2025 roadmap confirms consolidation of member and developer portals, with the new AP+ Member Portal starting with eftpos.
claims.quote: creating a single front door for members with a new AP+ Member Portal which has commenced with eftpos
claims.title: 2025 new AP+ Roadmap
claims.label: Verified

claims.claim: AP+ Developers replaced the separate NPP, BPAY and eftpos developer portals; existing users must reset passwords, and self-service sign-up exists.
claims.quote: If you were a user of the NPP, BPAY or eftpos developer portals, please reset your password using your registered email address.
claims.title: Australian Payments Plus Developers
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Nav: Products, APIs, Documentation, FAQs, Contact Us, Log In, Sign up (/auth/login?screen_hint=signup). /apis/, /faqs/ and /docs/ rendered no content logged out; /docs/ redirected to auth.developers.auspayplus.com.au. /products/ returned 404. No SDKs, sandbox, OpenAPI, versioning or rate-limit information readable logged out.

claims.claim: eftpos apps and API keys are issued through the AP+ developer portal, supported by apisupport@auspayplus.com.au.
claims.quote: eftpos apps and API keys are now available on the AP+ developer portal at developers.auspayplus.com.au.
claims.title: eftpos Australia - Support
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Support email decoded from Cloudflare-obfuscated mailto: apisupport@auspayplus.com.au.

claims.claim: AP+ publishes the eftpos interchange schedule (Current and Legacy tabs) by card type (Dual Network, Single Network, Prepaid) and category (Charity, Standard, DIFR 1-3, Strategic Rate 1, 2, 1&2); no effective date is shown on the page.
claims.quote: Interchange fees are payable between the retailer (known as a self-Acquirer) or the retailers’ financial institution (known as the Acquirer)
claims.title: Interchange fees - eftpos
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Dual Network Debit Cards, Standard column: 'In-Store Card > $10' shows $0.01 / $0.04; 'Card Not Present > $100' shows $0.10 and 0.12%; Transfers $0.045 in all non-charity categories. Note 1: 'Interchange Fees are not payable for Refunds and Declines.' Effective date absent on page.

claims.claim: Effective 1 December 2024 eftpos strategic interchange for eligible small business merchants fell to 2c per card-present transaction and 3c online.
claims.quote: Effective 1 December 2024, the interchange for all card present transactions, including mobile wallets, will reduce to 2c per transaction
claims.title: Rollout of Merchant Choice Routing for mobile devices plus lower eftpos debit charges will lower the cost of payments in Australia
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Eligibility criteria (e.g. minimum volume) apply; criteria not published.

claims.claim: From 1 May 2025 eftpos issuer scheme fees were cut 22% and acquirer scheme fees simplified to a single rate; fees otherwise unchanged since February 2022. Actual scheme fee amounts are not published.
claims.quote: Issuer scheme fees were lowered by 22%, while acquirer scheme fees were simplified to a single rate
claims.title: AP+ lowers eftpos scheme fees in ongoing commitment to lowering cost of payments
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Same article: 'eftpos scheme and interchange fees have not changed since February 2022'; LCR enabled for 70% of physical-card transactions and ~30% of Apple and Google wallets.

claims.claim: RBA finding cited by AP+: merchants with least-cost routing enabled pay nearly 20% less on debit transactions.
claims.quote: According to the Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA), businesses that enable LCR save nearly 20% on debit transactions²
claims.title: Merchant Choice Routing - eftpos
claims.label: Reported
claims.note: Footnote: The Effect of Least-cost Routing on Merchant Payment Costs, RBA Bulletin April 2024 (not fetched).

claims.claim: The RBA Payments System Board's 31 March 2026 Conclusions Paper removes surcharging on eftpos, Mastercard and Visa and lowers domestic interchange caps from 1 October 2026, with a foreign-card interchange cap from 1 April 2027.
claims.quote: Most of these changes will come into effect on 1 October 2026, including the removal of surcharging and reductions in the interchange caps
claims.title: Review of Merchant Card Payment Costs and Surcharging – Conclusions Paper | Media Releases | RBA
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Consultation Paper was July 2025. RBA to consult mid-2026 on mobile wallets, three-party networks, BNPL and e-commerce platforms.

claims.claim: eftpos, Mastercard and Visa are implementing no-surcharge rules from 1 October 2026 via cardsurcharge.com.au, coordinated by AusPayNet.
claims.quote: An initiative of eftpos, Mastercard and Visa, coordinated by Australian Payments Network, the industry body and self-regulator of payments in Australia.
claims.title: Card payment surcharging in Australia
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: AP+ support page: businesses that keep surcharging 'may be contacted by their bank or payment service provider' and 'may be subject to penalties'.

claims.claim: eftpos chargeback rights cover the losses required by ASIC's ePayments Code; scheme rules themselves are not published on the public site.
claims.quote: Yes. For eftpos transactions, chargeback rights cover the full range of losses required by the ePayments Code .
claims.title: eftpos Australia - Support
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Links to ASIC ePayments Code page. No public eftpos Scheme Rules document, edition or page count found.

claims.claim: Roadmap mandates: Click to Pay parity mandate for eftpos from 2027; 3DES-to-AES migration for Australian card payments by 2030; 3DS 2.3 support.
claims.quote: a parity mandate will come into effect from 2027 for institutions that support Click to Pay with international card schemes.
claims.title: 2025 new AP+ Roadmap
claims.label: Verified

claims.claim: Partner support channels are email-based: brand@auspayplus.com.au (branding/trade marks), apisupport@auspayplus.com.au (developer portal), payment_operations@auspayplus.com.au; merchants are directed to their acquirer, PSP or AP+ relationship manager. No hours or SLAs published.
claims.quote: To get started with MCR or for more information, contact your banking partner, payment service provider, or AP+ relationship manager.
claims.title: eftpos Australia - Support
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Email addresses decoded from Cloudflare-obfuscated mailto links on the page. AP+ Help Centre also linked in footer.

claims.claim: 26 September 2024: AP+ began rolling out Merchant Choice Routing for mobile-wallet transactions, progressively by handset and bank.
claims.quote: the rollout of Merchant Choice Routing (MCR) on transactions made via mobile wallets has now commenced
claims.title: Rollout of Merchant Choice Routing for mobile devices plus lower eftpos debit charges will lower the cost of payments in Australia
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Other dated items on the eftpos news list: 18 Dec 2024 and 30 Dec 2024 mobile-wallet technical update; 6 Mar 2025 Google Wallet LCR; 8 May 2025 scheme fee cut; 25 Aug 2025 scams; 22 Dec 2025 roadmap; 31 Jul 2026 roadmap; 11 Aug 2026 Western Union case study.

claims.claim: AP+ names Adrian Lovney as Chief Payments & Schemes Officer (May 2025), previously titled Chief Payments Officer (Sept 2024).
claims.quote: said Adrian Lovney, Chief Payments & Schemes Officer at AP+.
claims.title: AP+ lowers eftpos scheme fees in ongoing commitment to lowering cost of payments
claims.label: Verified

claims.claim: July 2026 roadmap: eftpos STIP Phase 2 added; NPP cloud migration date removed; Confirmation of Payee completed with over 100 institutions.
claims.quote: STIP Phase 2 introduces enhanced checks and verification capabilities that provide issuers with richer Stand-In Processing (STIP) functionality
claims.title: AP+ Roadmap (31 July 2026)
claims.label: Verified
